text:
Priya (PM): Heads-up — propose we onramp aurora-7 as EXPERIMENTAL with a 5% canary and soft pin policy. Reason: several small-mid customers asked for it, latency looks OK but cost is higher. Want quick consensus on bench gates + pin exceptions.
Ben (Eng): quick q — is aurora-7 available quantized? performance numbers we have are float16 only.
Priya (PM): not yet. Research said 4-bit quant may be possible but needs modelcard signoff. For canary we can use fp16.
Maria (SRE): p95 on our x1-small sim was ~230ms for 512 tokens when batched 4. Single-request p95 ~340ms (bad). We should gate on single-request p95 < 300ms for GA.
Tom (ProdOps): canary flow I propose: 5% -> 25% -> 100% if no regression in 48h windows. Rollback triggers: increased error rate >0.5% or p95 increase >20%.
Sasha (SE): BigCorp asked to pin for 6 months during migration. They will pay extra but need guaranteed latency. Pinning that long for experimental model seems risky. Any mitigation?
Izzy (Sales): BigCorp is willing to sign a T&M addendum + premium. They care mostly about inference cost vs existing model. If we offer a 3-month pin with performance credits, they might take it.
Ben (Eng): mitigation idea: soft-stable pin that routes to aurora-7 for their tenant but falls back to aurora-7-small (lower-cost variant) under SLO pressure. Implement via routing policy with `fallback_model`.
Priya (PM): that sounds reasonable. Proposed bench gates: p95_single < 300ms, reg_eval_pass_rate >= 95%, token_cost <= $0.14/1k. Also require quant plan within 8 weeks for GA.
Ben (Eng): sample catalog config for discussion:
```json
{
  "model_id": "aurora-7",
  "entry_type": "experimental",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "pin_policy": "soft-stable",
  "fallback_model": "aurora-7-small",
  "bench_gates": {
    "p95_single_ms": 300,
    "eval_pass_rate": 0.95,
    "cost_usd_per_1k_tokens": 0.14
  },
  "canary_escalation": [5,25,100],
  "rollback_triggers": {"error_rate_pct": 0.5, "p95_increase_pct": 20}
}
```
Sasha (SE): we should also add a per-tenant opt-out flag for BigCorp if they insist on hard pin. That would require infra and legal signoff.
Maria (SRE): ops note — prefix/KV cache behavior differs across variants. If we soft-pin, ensure cache keys include model variant to avoid cross-tenant cache leakage.
Tom (ProdOps): agree. Also we need observability: per-tenant p95, token cost, and a daily regression diff against baseline model. Otherwise we can't guard customer SLAs.
Izzy (Sales): action: I'll ask BigCorp if 3 months + performance credit is acceptable and flag any hard-deadline launch dates.
Priya (PM): decision items: (1) agree bench gates above, (2) allow soft-stable pin with fallback, (3) sales to negotiate 3mo pin option, (4) eng to deliver quant plan in 8w. Approve? :thumbsup: or :eyes: to block.
Ben (Eng): :thumbsup: from eng. I'll take ownership of quant plan + canary automation.
Maria (SRE): :thumbsup: ops will own rollout monitoring and rollback playbook.
Sasha (SE): :eyes: need legal on per-tenant hard pin exceptions.
Izzy (Sales): :thumbsup: I'll update BigCorp and confirm commitment.
Priya (PM): thanks — I'll write the RFC and add the catalog entry template. Targeting internal canary next Tue.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: model-catalog entry draft created for aurora-7 (id=mc-aurora7-draft).
Tom (ProdOps): quick follow-up — can we set automatic cost-throttling to kick in if token_cost > $0.16/1k for 1hr? prevents runaway bills.
Ben (Eng): we can add a runtime policy with cost-throttle threshold. I'll add to canary config.
Priya (PM): great. We'll reconvene after sales check-in. Closing thread for now. :party_parrot:
